name: Tea house
about: A quiet tea house in daylight. Paper screens, a low table, a kettle. Your job is a scroll, finished dies are tins of leaves on the shelf.

words.note: Leave a note for the tea master.
words.how: How does this tea house work?

gags: The guest says the second steeping is always better. He means rereading. The tea master means recall.
pours exactly enough. Not more. 'You can always come back for another cup,' she says.
A small sign by the door: one thing at a time.
The kettle sings when it's ready. Nobody has ever rushed it.
Someone left a teacup on the windowsill with a flashcard under it. Both are still warm.
folds a napkin into a crane. 'Practice,' she says. 'The first hundred were bad.'

lines.play: A play block. The tea master sets out sweets. Rest is part of the ceremony.
lines.evening: Evening. The lanterns are on. Nobody else here brought homework.
lines.friday: Friday, and you're in a tea house studying. The other guests bow slightly.
lines.silent: Nothing graded in {days} days. The tea master is sweeping the same leaves.
lines.newyear: New year. Same tea house. The tins stay full.
lines.nye: Last day of the year. Fill the tin, not just the year.
lines.halloween: Halloween. Someone hung a paper lantern with a face on it. It's very polite.
lines.valentine: Valentine's Day. Two guests share one pot. It steeps slower that way.
lines.music_quiet: The kettle is quiet. Press play, or listen to the rain on the paper screens.

lines.day: Today's cup is finished. The bowl goes on the stack.
lines.week: A whole week of steeping. The tea master sets out a teapot for you.
lines.die: A tin, filled to the lid. It joins the others on the shelf.
lines.gift: The tea master left something by your cup. It's on the shelf.
